CLINICAL FEATURES OF VARICELLA (CHICKENPOX)
Clinical Features
- Incubation period is 10 - 21 days
- Vesicular eruptions consist of delicate "teardrop" vesicles on an
erythematous base
- The eruption starts with faint macules that develop rapidly into vesicles
within 24 hours
- Successive fresh crops of vesicles appear for a few days, mainly on the
trunk, face, and oral mucosa
- New lesions usually stop appearing by the fifth day; the majority is crusted
by the sixth day
- Most disappear in less than 20 days without a scar, except larger and
secondarily infected lesions
- Low grade fever
- Malaise
- Headaches
- The severity of the disease is age-dependent
- Adults have more severe disease and a greater risk of visceral disease
